messages:
ana: Hey team - getting pile-on from multiple customers reporting 5xx errors from the hosted inference API since ~2026-03-15T10:17Z. High level: control-plane is returning 502/503s that look like upstream dependency timeouts (auth/session, routing-policy, config DB). Example error from customer payload: `503 Service Unavailable - controlplane: routing-policy fetch failed: context deadline exceeded (configdb)`

support-bot: ALERT: control-plane error-rate (5xx) spike detected for cluster-prod in us-west-2. 1m error_rate=12.8% (threshold 2%). See https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/ctrlplane-5xx-1975

ana: Attached customer example: correlation_id=cid-0a1b2c3d, request_id=req-9f8e7d6c, sample headers: `x-rw-account: acct-4512`, `x-rw-model: gpt-open-7b`. Customer says: "requests fail intermittently, retries sometimes succeed after ~8-12s"

mike: oncall here. Thanks Ana. Can you paste the raw error (stack/log) from the control-plane response body? Also which sub-service is failing (auth vs routing vs configdb) per the trace?

ana: Raw response snippet: ```{\n  "error": "upstream_timeout",\n  "service": "routing-policy",\n  "cause": "configdb query timed out",\n  "duration_ms": 10305,\n  "correlation_id": "cid-0a1b2c3d"\n}```

noah: I'm seeing increased p99 latency on configdb queries and elevated `DB_CONN_WAIT` in the routing-policy service logs. Stack trace lines: ``router.go:142 handleRequest -> policycache.go:88 fetchPolicy -> configdb/sql.go:213 queryContext ctx deadline exceeded``. Looks like connection saturation + slow queries.

tyler: Checking infra: config-db (postgres-repl) CPU/IO looks fine, but active connections spiked from 120 -> 480 around 10:15Z, and connection_pool waiters rose. Could be a storm of concurrent control-plane lookups after a cache eviction.

mike: Action plan (quick): 1) enable routing-policy fail-open so control-plane can serve best-effort routing instead of blocking; 2) increase DB query timeout from 2s -> 10s temporarily; 3) roll routing-policy pods one-by-one to pick up config changes; 4) throttle bursty clients if needed. Any objections?

noah: Agree. Also suggest enabling prefix/KV cache warmup for routing-policy to avoid immediate large fanout to configdb. I can deploy a patch to prefer in-memory fallback if DB times out.

ana: Repro steps from customer (they provided): 1) send 10 concurrent generate requests with long prompts (~1.5k tokens) 2) include `session-id` header 3) observe 502/503 within 5-15s 

mike: Executed commands: `kubectl -n controlplane get pods -l app=routing-policy` -> restarted one pod: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/routing-policy -n controlplane --token-restart` (rolled 1/5). Also applied config flag `ROUTING_FAIL_OPEN=true` via configmap patch and bumped `DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` from 2000 -> 10000.

sre-bot: Deploy event: rollout/routing-policy restarted by mike at 2026-03-15T10:28:12Z. Change set: set ROUTING_FAIL_OPEN, DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS=10000.

noah: After restart and config changes, 5xx count dropped from 13% -> 1.6% in 3m. Logs show fewer `queryContext deadline exceeded` entries. Still seeing occasional auth session timeouts for one tenant (acct-4512). Investigating session-store latency.

tyler: For the session-store issue looks like the session cache (redis) had a short failover event 10:12Z that caused some keys to be missed, which triggered auth lookups against configdb. That correlated with the initial fanout. Redis metrics show a failover completed ~10:14Z.

ana: Customer update sent: "we're seeing intermittent 5xx earlier today, our traffic is back to normal after your workaround - thanks". They requested a postmortem and whether there's an ETA for permanent fix.

mike: Next steps / action items: - noah to implement longer-term fallback in routing-policy (preferred: in-memory TTLed policy cache + async refresh) - tyler to add DB connection limits + better pooling + better instrumentation for waiter counts - infra to add an automated circuit-breaker to fail-open if configdb latency > 500ms for 30s - support to draft customer-facing summary

noah: I'll open PR for fallback cache and add a feature flag `routing_policy_inmem_fallback`. Target: hotfix branch -> canary -> prod within 48 hours.

tyler: I'll increase connection pool max to 800 temporarily and tune keepalives + add alert for `DB_CONN_WAIT > 200` meaning slowdowns.

mike: Closing loop: error_rate stable at ~0.8% now, predominant remaining hits are single-tenant auth session timeouts that correlate with redis failover. Marking incident as mitigated. Please add detailed timelines to the incident tracker and assign owners for the follow-ups.

ana: Thanks all. I'll create a customer-facing note and a draft postmortem. Putting link here once ready. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident MITIGATED: ctrlplane-5xx-spike-1975123456. Severity: Pager->Med. Created incident: https://incidents.redwood.internal/1975123456

mike: Nice work. We'll keep this thread open for the postmortem link and final RCA.

ana: Postmortem draft: `https://docs.redwood.internal/postmortems/ctrlplane-5xx-spike-1975123456.md` (wip). Closing thread when doc published.
